name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,591

clue.text: Each head's scratched fiercely

indicators.note: scratching out the head of a word removes its opening letter

blocks.note: each and every are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone is scratching their scalp hard, every head being clawed at furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: EVERY loses its first letter to leave VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as intensifying adverbs meaning extremely or to a great degree.

clue.text: Strong old soldier captures macho blokes

indicators.note: a captor holds its prisoner inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a vet is a veteran, an old soldier
he-men are macho blokes

explanation.surface: A tough veteran soldier takes some muscular men prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement feelings or arguments are forceful and intense, so powerful in that sense.

clue.text: Yellow topped black

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its top, and in a down clue that is its first letter

blocks.note: yellow means cowardly, and craven is a synonym

explanation.surface: It reads like a colour description: something yellow on top of something black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour beside 'black', but it means cowardly here; CRAVEN loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Raven as an adjective describes glossy jet-dark hair, like the plumage of the bird.

clue.text: Stretch bra out of shape? Nothing is revealed when it's pressed

definitions.text: Nothing is revealed when it's pressed

indicators.note: something pulled out of shape has lost its form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a stretch of time or ground is a space
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An overstretched bra is pressed and nothing shows, a risque wardrobe joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition pretends to be about modesty; pressing the long key on a keyboard reveals only blank space.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the long keyboard key inserts a blank gap, so the visible result on screen is empty.

clue.text: Folded page and left to dine with editor

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
L is the abbreviation for left
to dine is to eat
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper story: a page is folded and someone leaves to have dinner with the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleated skirt has fabric pressed into regular folds, so creased or doubled over.

clue.text: Gang perhaps developing cult with no violence

indicators.note: something developing is changing form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gang turns into a cult that renounces violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gang' looks like criminals, but here it is a word for a group, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gang is a grammatical term for a group noun like flock or herd, so an example of the category.

clue.text: Attack American woman on team

blocks.note: broad is American slang for a woman
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: An American woman launches an attack on her own team.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a forceful verbal assault, originally the firing of all guns on one side of a warship.

clue.text: Regretted being offensive on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard rather than read, so the sound matters

blocks.note: rude means offensive

explanation.surface: A broadcaster regrets having been offensive on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to feel sorry about it, so the past tense means felt sorry for.

clue.text: Deception involving secret plan with fees

indicators.note: to involve is to entangle or twist together, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A con involving a hidden scheme for extracting fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining money by false pretences is the legal phrase for fraud through misrepresentation, so trickery.

clue.text: Den is after peach, oddly leaving cake

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters depart, so only the even-placed ones stay
this places one piece behind the other in the finished word

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of peach
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a peach for a piece of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Be unbalanced as cow almost leaves horse rattled

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word after it is dropped
something rattled is shaken about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene: a cow wanders off and the horse is spooked and unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAVES loses its S before the fifteen letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be slightly crazy or mentally unstable, like a machine missing a fixing.

clue.text: Passage for those who are boring?

definitions.text: Passage for those who are boring?

blocks.clueFragment: Passage for those who are boring?
blocks.note: surface reading: a corridor or passage of text meant for dull people
setter's reading: boring means drilling into the ground, so the passage is a tunnel dug by excavators

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests tedious people, but it means digging; the passage is a vertical tunnel for miners.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners drill into the earth, and the vertical tunnel they use to reach the coal seam is that passage.

clue.text: Conclusions from The Guardian panned Boris's aims

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their last letters, taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A newspaper review: The Guardian criticised the ambitions of Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclusions' looks like the definition, but it is the selection signal; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are goals or purposes, as in 'the end justifies the means', so objectives.

clue.text: Poor hen shifting - one's likely to lay an egg

definitions.text: one's likely to lay an egg

indicators.note: shifting letters move to new positions, so the word order is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sorry hen shuffles about, the bird most likely to lay an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: To lay an egg is an idiom for failing badly, so the hen picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, and laying an egg is slang for flopping.

clue.text: Game husband having drink after work

indicators.note: after places the drink behind the other pieces in the finished word

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
an op, short for opus, is a work
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: A husband has a whisky after work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground pastime of hopping through squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Particular dock?

blocks.note: first meaning: an individual item or point, as in a fine point
second meaning, read cryptically: to dock is to cut off a tail

explanation.walkthrough: To dock an animal is to cut its tail, so the answer is read as DE-TAIL, remove the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is a single item of information, and docking an animal removes its tail.

clue.text: Wants no yen for pay

indicators.note: no means without, so the following item is removed

blocks.note: wants are longings or yearnings
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone longs for wages but receives no Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money received from work, so wages or salary.

clue.text: Sons go before church sermon

indicators.note: before places the first pieces ahead of the last in the finished word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to go is a euphemism for to urinate
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Boys head off before church, or use the loo before the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' in the toilet sense is a cheeky euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a talk delivered from the pulpit, so a formal address.

clue.text: Gentleman concealed a large repair

blocks.note: concealed means hid
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
to repair to a place is to go there

explanation.surface: A gentleman hides a big repair job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair' suggests mending, but it is the old sense of retiring somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish nobleman of the lower rank, a gentleman by birth.

clue.text: Shannon maybe embracing one by a holiday destination

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps around another
by means next to, placing the final piece beside the rest

blocks.note: the Shannon is Ireland's longest river
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Shannon cuddles up to a person at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shannon' looks like a woman's name but is the Irish river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the Mediterranean coastline of France and Italy, a classic seaside resort area.

clue.text: Discover the truth about low noise

blocks.note: first meaning: to see through or find out a person or scheme
second meaning: a deep continuous rolling sound, as of thunder

explanation.walkthrough: Rumble in the first sense is informal British for finding someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally one can expose a deception that way, and the noun also names the deep growl of thunder.

clue.text: Spots Mickelson finally securing hole-in-one? On the contrary

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the golfer's name
to secure is to hold fast, so one piece is placed inside another
this flips the roles, so the outer and inner pieces swap from what the surface says

blocks.note: an ace in golf is a hole played in a single stroke
Phil Mickelson is an American golfer

explanation.surface: Golfer Phil Mickelson finally lands a hole-in-one, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the golfer's letter holds the ace; 'On the contrary' means the ace holds the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition causing pimples, so a crop of blemishes on the face.

clue.text: Weak with emotional strain? Not the first aspect

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is left off

blocks.note: dim can mean faint or weak
tension is emotional strain

explanation.surface: Someone feels feeble under nervous stress.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimension is a facet or feature of a situation, as in a new side to the problem.

clue.text: It might be used to cover cake in picnic in garden

definitions.text: It might be used to cover cake

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: Something used to coat a cake at an outdoor picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: Frosting or sugar glaze is spread over a sponge as a decorative top layer.

clue.text: Very plump bottom goes on this?

definitions.text: Very plump bottom goes on this?

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, and it goes away

blocks.note: so means very, as in so tired
plump means fat

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about where a very large backside sits.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a big bottom sits on a couch.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is furniture people sit on, so a broad backside naturally rests there.

clue.text: Abandoned soul in political vision

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forsaken spirit lost in a grand political dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A vision can be something seen that is not really there, like a trick of the eye.

clue.text: Bond's wound is on head

indicators.note: wound here is the past of wind, so the letters are twisted round

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: James Bond has an injury on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like the spy and 'wound' like an injury; the noun bond is the definition and wound rhymes with sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is sticking together, so a bond in the sense of a join between surfaces.

clue.text: Gets old, wise person to move south

indicators.note: south points to the compass letter, which travels from the front to the back of the word

blocks.note: a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: An elderly wise man retires to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SAGE moves to the end to give AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older, so the third-person verb means becomes elderly.
